slides.title: School and Learning
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 3 English, Unit 2: School and Learning. This unit is all about school and learning. You will talk about your lessons, your teacher, and the subjects you study, like mathematics and grammar. You will learn the words for the supplies you use every day, such as an eraser and your books. You will find out how to get ready for a contest, write a short report, and use the library well. Best of all, you will learn to talk about things that happened in the past — what you studied, where you went, and why you enjoyed it. By the end, you will be ready to cheer for the Grammar Champions in this unit’s story! In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Name the people, places, and supplies at school, using words like teacher, library, and eraser.
Talk about your school subjects, such as mathematics and grammar, and say which you prefer.
Tell about things that happened before, using the simple past tense (studied, prepared, went).
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to name the people, places, and supplies at school, using words like teacher, library, and eraser. You will also talk about your school subjects, such as mathematics and grammar, and say which you prefer. You will also tell about things that happened before, using the simple past tense (studied, prepared, went). Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Words to learn
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: teacher, author, library, graduate, mathematics, grammar. Listen to each word, look at what it means, and try to use it when you talk and write.

slides.title: Read and think
bullets: Point to the words that show it
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes A Day at School and Getting Ready for the Contest. Read slowly, look at the pictures, and find the big idea in each text. When you answer a question, point to the words that show it.

slides.title: The Simple Past Tense
bullets: We use the simple past tense to talk about things that already happened — yesterday, last week, or a long time ago. It helps us tell stories and say what...
Try it in your own sentences
slides.narration: The first language focus is The Simple Past Tense. We use the simple past tense to talk about things that already happened — yesterday, last week, or a long time ago. It helps us tell stories and say what we did. Look at the examples, then try the pattern in your own sentences.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Speaking 1 — Talk About Your School Day
Say it, write it, make it better
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1 — Talk About Your School Day. Say your ideas clearly and listen to your partner. In writing, you will draw, trace, copy or write, then check your work with a grown-up or the AI tutor.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the words, then the reading and the questions, then the grammar, speaking and writing. Ask the AI tutor for help any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
